newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM says to cut Rauma stake below 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: UPM says to cut Rauma stake below 50 pct.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy said on Tuesday it planned to reduce its holding in engineering group Rauma Oy to below 50 percent from the current 73 percent.

UPM-Kymmene earlier said in a statement with its 1996 results that it would pay 3.00 markka of its 4.50 markka 1996 dividend in Rauma shares. The share dividend would reduce UPM's stake in Rauma to 59.9 percent, UPM-Kymmene said.
"In the future it is intended to reduce this (stake) to below 50 percent," UPM-Kymmene said.
Shareholders with fewer than 500 UPM-Kymmene shares would receive the dividend entirely in cash, but would also have the option to buy Rauma shares with their dividend, UPM said.

The Rauma shares would be valued at 107.74 markka per share, which is the average trade-weighted quotation on the Helsinki bourse from February 1 to February 28, 1997, less Rauma's proposed 2.75 markka dividend, UPM said.
Shareholders with more than 500 UPM shares would receive one Rauma share for every 35.91 UPM share held, with the undivisible excess paid in cash, UPM said.

Shareholders with fewer than 500 shares would be able to buy between one and 13 Rauma shares per book entry from May 6 to 19, UPM said. However, the offer would not apply to shareholders in the U.S., it said.
